rounds.text: Akanksha Power & Infrastructure Ltd demonstrates robust core expansion, highlighted by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 26% and profit growth of 25% [E14, E16], alongside stellar recent metrics including YoY net profit surging by 70% [E49] and a 16% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E17]. Operational efficiency is visibly strengthening, with the yearly operating-margin trend increasing over the last 4 years [E23], TTM operating margin expanding to 14% (+4 percentage points) [E21], and quarterly operating margin reaching 16% in September 2026 (+5 percentage points) [E22]. Cash generation remains exceptionally high quality, underpinned by a Mar 2026 cash conversion ratio of 1.74x where profits are fully backed by operating cash flow of Rs 10.18 Cr [E25, E26]. Furthermore, working capital management has seen a major structural breakthrough, with debtor days dramatically improving from 162 down to 97.2 days [E42], while capital expenditure is actively scaling via a 43.0% YoY increase in capital-work-in-progress to Rs 6.15 Cr [E31]. On relative valuation metrics, the stock trades at discounts to sector benchmarks, including a P/E of 19.28x versus 21.1x [E6], a P/B of 1.6x versus 2.32x [E7], and an EV/EBITDA of 11.98x versus 12.14x [E11]. Conceded: the stock trades at an elevated standalone P/E of 57.3x and a price-to-book of 4.45x alongside a negative free cash flow of Rs -21.43 Cr [E1, E2, E27].

Akanksha Power & Infrastructure trades at an expensive valuation of 57.3x P/E [E1] and 4.45x P/B [E2, E43], leaving the stock overvalued with a -39.9% margin of safety as DCF intrinsic value stands at Rs 127 per share against the market price of Rs 177 [E36, E37, E51]. This valuation disconnect is driven by market sentiment running ahead of execution, with 1-year price growth of 127% [E18] outpacing profit growth by 111% [E40] and requiring a 22.7% implied earnings growth rate versus the 18.0% base case [E38]. Such rich multiples are unjustified given weak capital efficiency, as seen in a 3-year median ROE of just 8% [E19, E45] and current ROE of 8.4% [E13], both trailing the sector benchmark of 11.35% [E9]. Cash flows show underlying strain as free cash flow sat at Rs -21.43 Cr in Mar 2026 [E27], while borrowings expanded to Rs 54.55 Cr in Sep 2026 [E30] and dividend yield remains 0.00% [E4, E44]. Furthermore, sales growth over the trailing twelve months contracted to -3% [E15], coinciding with promoter equity falling to 57.51% [E32] and both foreign and domestic institutional holdings dropping to 0.00% [E33, E34]. Conceded: operating cash flow reached Rs 10.18 Cr in Mar 2026 [E26] with cash conversion at 1.74x [E25], alongside an increasing operating margin trend reaching 14% TTM [E21, E23].

Conceded: the DCF intrinsic value is Rs 127 versus the market price of Rs 177 [E36], and trailing twelve-month sales growth contracted by -3% [E15]. However, the bear's focus on high multiples ignores relative sector value, where the stock actually trades at a discount on P/E of 19.28x versus the sector benchmark of 21.1x [E6], and a P/B of 1.6x against a sector benchmark of 2.32x [E7]. The claim of weak capital efficiency and cash strain is directly countered by robust cash generation, evidenced by a cash conversion ratio of 1.74x with operating cash flow reaching Rs 10.18 Cr in Mar 2026 [E25, E26], alongside a massive structural improvement in debtor days from 162 down to 97.2 days [E42]. Operating margins are expanding rather than stalling, demonstrating a rising yearly trend with TTM operating margins reaching 14% compared to 10% three years prior [E21, E23], and quarterly margins hitting 16% in Sep 2026 [E22]. Furthermore, the bear's dismissal of growth ignores strong recent performance flags showing net profit surging 70% YoY [E49] and 3-year compounded profit growth at 25% [E16], paired with active capital expenditure visible in a 43.0% increase in CWIP to Rs 6.15 Cr [E31].

The bull’s reliance on sector benchmarks [E6, E7] is misleading because it ignores the company’s own high absolute valuation of 57.3x P/E [E1] and 4.45x P/B [E2], which the company itself flags as a negative [E43]. While the bull highlights cash conversion [E25], it fails to address the critical reality that free cash flow was negative at Rs -21.43 Cr in Mar 2026 [E27], indicating that reported profits are not translating into actual liquidity. Conceded: the company has improved debtor days [E42] and expanded operating margins [E21, E22]. However, this operational progress is overshadowed by the fact that institutional investors have completely exited the stock, with foreign and domestic holdings dropping to 0.00% [E33, E34]. Finally, the reliance on CWIP [E31] as a sign of strength is premature, as the company is simultaneously increasing its debt burden to Rs 54.55 Cr [E30] while failing to provide any dividend return to shareholders [E4, E44].
